model: Sum-of-the-parts: owner-FCF DCF of the consolidated non-property operating businesses (engine route) plus listed stakes in Swire Properties and Cathay Pacific at market value, less holdco net debt and NCI

inputs.share_count_basis: 'B'-share-equivalent count = 'A' shares x 5 + 'B' shares (each A carries 5x the economic/dividend entitlement of a B; equal votes per share). H1 2026 note 11 (0087.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt lines 3624-3625, 4127): 778,988,000 A x 5 + 2,848,932,500 B = 6,743.9m, unchanged 1 Jan-30 Jun 2026; matches core_metrics H1 FY2026 shares 6,742. Identical economic base to 0019.HK's 1,348.7m A-equivalents (x5 = 6,743.5m; the 0.006% gap is 0019's dividend-implied rounding). No dilutive securities, no SBC; held flat. No buyback in H1 2026 (FY2025 HK$1,851m, FY2024 HK$3,878m under the completed HK$6bn programme).
inputs.net_debt_basis: HOLDCO / NON-PROPERTY net debt only, 30 June 2026 segment note 1(c) and 1(b): external borrowings Head Office 35,369 + HAECO 168 = 35,537; less bank balances Beverages 7,242 + HAECO 1,502 + T&I 673 + Head Office 3,406 = 12,823. Swire Properties' own borrowings (49,221) and cash (9,424) are excluded because the SP stake enters at its market capitalisation, which is already net of SP's debt. Ties to consolidated net debt: 22,714 + (49,221 - 9,424) = 62,511 = reported 30 Jun 2026 net debt. Includes the HK$4.7bn Cathay exchangeable bond issued 16 June 2026. Lease liabilities EXCLUDED (treatment B, leases charged in the flows).
inputs.fcf_scope_note: last_fcf/reported_fcf are the modelled-scope (non-property operating businesses, ex-Cathay) TTM June-2026 owner FCF estimate: EBITDA ~7,790 - lease cash ~1,180 - cash tax ~830 - capex ~4,600 = ~1,180. Consolidated group FCF (incl. Swire Properties, FY2025) was HK$6,998m (OCF 14,551 - capex incl. investment property 7,553) and is NOT the base of this model.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not deducted: the modelled scope carries net DEBT (HK$22.7bn), not net cash. Group interest income HK$610m FY2025 sits in finance income below EBITDA, outside the flows.
inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero market: Swire Pacific runs no material equity-settled share scheme (no share-based payment line in the FY2025 consolidated cash flow statement or segment notes); SBC rows kept explicit at 0%.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 share repurchases HK$1,851m (H1 2025 HK$1,847m), FY2024 HK$3,878m -- the HK$6bn programme announced 2024. None in H1 2026. Value-neutral in this model; count held flat.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T08:08:05Z (HKEX regular close, Friday; Yahoo chart API, 0087.HK B-share quote)
inputs.base_revenue_note: Non-property external revenue, TTM to 30 June 2026: FY2025 (90,467 - Property 15,992 = 74,475) + H1 2026 (49,446 - 9,386 = 40,060) - H1 2025 (45,774 - 8,699 = 37,075) = 77,460. Beverages ~44.3bn, HAECO ~25.5bn, Trading & Industrial ~7.7bn, Healthcare/Head Office ~0.4bn. TTM rather than FY2025 so the flows start where the June 2026 balance sheet ends.
inputs.wacc_rationale: HKD-built (HKD pegged to USD). Risk-free 4.0% (HK/US 10y), ERP 5.5%, beta 0.85 on the operating mix (consumer staples bottler + MRO + retail/motors) -> cost of equity ~8.7%; cost of debt 3.4% (H1 2026 weighted average) x (1-16.5%) = 2.8%; ~80/20 E/D at the holdco -> ~7.5%, rounded UP to 8.0% for the Chinese Mainland/SE Asia consumer and FX translation exposure embedded in Beverages. Identical in all three scenarios: risk is carried in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: lease cash (principal ~1,000 + interest ~185 for the non-property businesses, from group principal 1,041 and lease interest 204 in FY2025 less Swire Properties' small share) charged as lease_cost_pct_path 1.5% inside the flows; D&A path is EX right-of-use depreciation (4.1% vs ~5.4% incl. ROU) so cash-tax EBIT is not charged twice; non-property lease liabilities (Beverages 1,138, HAECO 2,485, T&I 834, HO 8 = 4,465 at 30 Jun 2026) EXCLUDED from net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated (pre-NCI); NCI deducted ONCE in the equity bridge at estimated value (HK$11.15bn): book NCI of Beverages 7,709 + HAECO 1,882 + Aviation other 101 = 9,692 at 30 Jun 2026 (segment note 1(c)), marked up ~15% to ~13x the ~HK$800-850m/yr NCI profit share run-rate (H1 2026: Beverages PAT 1,012 vs attributable 846; HAECO 890 vs 653). Swire Properties' 16.69% NCI is not deducted because the SP stake enters at 83.31% of market cap, not 100%.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE (same as 0019.HK): Swire Pacific straddles three routing rows -- a holdco whose largest asset (83.31% of Swire Properties) is an IAS-40 landlord, a 45.12% equity-accounted airline associate (Cathay), and wholly-controlled operating businesses (Swire Coca-Cola, HAECO, Trading & Industrial). Per SKILL.md ('when a ticker straddles two rows, value the parts separately and sum'), this is a SUM-OF-THE-PARTS: (1) the consolidated non-property operating businesses are an owner-FCF DCF through the engine (owner-fcf.md + adaptations: HKD WACC, lease treatment B, NCI in bridge, SBC-zero); (2) the two listed stakes enter the equity bridge at market value (Swire Properties 1972.HK, Cathay 0293.HK, Yahoo closes 2026-10-09); (3) holdco net debt excludes Swire Properties' debt because SP enters at its equity value. Consolidated reported net income and EPS are NOT used: they are dominated by investment-property fair-value movements (HK$-6.1bn FY2025) and Cathay's equity-accounted profit; neither is a cash flow to the holdco and the SOTP values both assets directly. Head Office costs (~HK$-0.64bn/yr TTM operating, plus Healthcare losses) are inside the modelled EBITDA, so the capitalised holdco cost is charged once against the whole group. Interim dividend payable (HK$2,023m, ex 9 Sep, paid 9 Oct 2026) and the 2026 interim dividends receivable from Swire Properties and Cathay (also ex before the valuation date, received after 30 June) are treated as offsetting and both omitted. No prior DCF for 0087.HK; first valuation. SHARE CLASS: this file values the 'B' shares (0087.HK) of the same consolidated group valued in 0019.HK (the 'A' shares), built the same day from the same filings, flows, equity bridge, weights and prices of the listed stakes. Only the divisor differs: 6,743.9m B-equivalents vs 1,348.7m A-equivalents, so every per-share value here is 1/5 of 0019.HK's (to rounding). EPS/DPS/shares in core_metrics are already on the B basis and were not rescaled. MARKET: B closed at 15.00 = 75.00 per A-equivalent against the A share's 102.10 at the same close, a ~27% discount for identical economics. The discount reflects B-share illiquidity and the fact that the B class is ~70% held by John Swire & Sons (which controls ~52% of votes through it), leaving a small free float -- it is a liquidity/control discount, not a different claim on cash flows. For an outside investor the B share is the cheaper way to own the same economics. SANITY-CHECK FIX (2026-10-11, one pass): the first build valued the SOTP at full look-through (weighted HK$24.38/B, implied P/B 0.635x vs a 10-year ceiling of 0.40x; sanity_check tripped). Diagnosis: a structural holding-company discount, not the operating DCF. The listed stakes (~77% of gross asset value) are already marked at their own market prices, so a WACC premium or the 1.5% growth cap on the operating businesses alone moves the value by ~HK$1-2/B share and cannot close a ~HK$1.4bn-per-0.01x P/B gap of this size. Fix: an explicit 35% holdco discount to SOTP NAV in equity_bridge, anchored on the 10-year P/B ceiling. WACC 8%, growth, margin, capex and tax paths, weights and the stake marks are all deliberately UNCHANGED.

equity_bridge.note: 83.31% x 5,757,484,800 SP shares (FY2025 AR principal subsidiaries list, line 11569) = 4,796.6m shares x HK$24.44 (Yahoo close 2026-10-09). Market cap is net of SP's own HK$39.8bn net debt. SP trades at roughly half its own reported NAV; marking at market rather than NAV is the deliberately conservative choice given HK office oversupply.

2,743.8m Cathay shares (43.09% x 6,722.9m pre-buyback = 2,896.9m; Qatar 9.56% buy-back 24 Feb 2026 lifts Swire to 47.64%; placing of 153.06m at HK$11.74 on 12 Mar 2026 -> 45.12%, H1 2026 note 13) x HK$14.12 (Yahoo close 2026-10-09). Tie: 30 Jun 2026 market value HK$35,613m disclosed = HK$12.98/share implied.

equity_bridge.item: Exchangeable bond: in-the-money value ceded to holders
equity_bridge.note: HK$4.7bn bond (in holdco debt) exchangeable into 356.6m Cathay shares at HK$13.18; Cathay at HK$14.12 -> (14.12-13.18) x 356.6m = HK$335m of the stake's upside belongs to bondholders. Matures 16 Jun 2027.

equity_bridge.item: HAECO and Beverages JV/associate earnings (HAESL/TEXL engine JVs etc.) at 11x
equity_bridge.note: Equity-accounted, so excluded from the modelled EBITDA; matching asset per adaptations (d). TTM share of JV profit HAECO 548 (FY25 530 + H1'26 270 - H1'25 252) + Beverages 67 = 615 post-tax x 11. Book value of these JVs ~4.0bn (HAECO 2,448 + Bev 1,558).

Head Office/Healthcare associated companies (Columbia China, New Frontier GBA, IHC) carrying value 30 Jun 2026, segment note 1(b). Loss-making (-67 FY2025) so book, not earnings. Aviation 'Others' assets (3,812 segment + 2,137 JV, ~nil earnings, largely consolidation adjustments) deliberately given no value.

equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interests in consolidated operating businesses
equity_bridge.note: See inputs.nci_treatment: book 9,692 marked to ~1.15x / ~13x NCI earnings.

35% x base-scenario undiscounted SOTP equity HK$164,232m (2026-10-11 build: EV 34,879 + bridge 152,068 - holdco net debt 22,714) = HK$57,481m = HK$8.52/B share, applied as a fixed HK$ amount in all three scenarios (the engine's bridge is scenario-invariant; the discount is a property of the ownership structure, not of the operating flows). EMPIRICAL ANCHOR: 0087.HK's year-end P/B has never exceeded 0.40x in ten years (FY2017 0.3985x; range 0.215-0.399x, average 0.303x, sanity_check 2026-10-10). The undiscounted SOTP implied 0.62-0.64x book, a rating the market has never granted. 1 - 0.40/0.617 = 35%: the discount that puts the base value at the 10-year P/B ceiling. It sits inside the 30-50% range at which HK family-controlled conglomerates (Jardine Matheson, CK Hutchison, Swire's own A/B history) trade to look-through NAV with listed stakes at market. Not a WACC adjustment: the operating DCF keeps its 8% HKD rate.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (~0%) diverges >30% from revenue and EPS CAGRs, and none is a clean growth signal: equity is flattened by investment-property revaluation losses (HK$-6.0bn FY2024, -6.1bn FY2025) and the HK$11.32/A special dividend in 2023; revenue is distorted by the SCCU (US bottler) sale Sep-2023, TNCC (Thailand) consolidation Sep-2024 and HAECO Americas sale Nov-2025; EPS 5-yr is undefined (FY2020 loss -7.32) and EPS 3-yr compares a 2.81 base to a 2.17 year depressed by fair-value losses. Underlying profit 3-yr (+33.8%) starts from a COVID-depressed FY2022. Forward growth is therefore built bottom-up from the non-property segments, not from a historical CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF (SBC zero; interest income not deducted because the group is net debt). FCF 3-yr CAGR undefined: FY2022 consolidated FCF was negative (-2,054) during the Swire Properties investment-property capex peak. Recurring underlying profit FY2023 10,449 -> FY2024 9,284 -> FY2025 9,754 -> H1 2026 6,962 (+48% YoY). EPS on the B basis: FY2022 0.56 -> FY2025 0.43 (3-yr -8.4%); FY2020 loss -1.46 leaves the 5-yr undefined. H1 2026 B EPS 1.00 (vs 0.12 H1 2025, which carried the Cathay/HAECO Americas and revaluation losses).

base.ebitda_margin_rationale: TTM non-property EBITDA ~7,790 on 77,460 = 10.1%: Swire Coca-Cola operating EBITDA 5,152 (11.8%), HAECO ~3,090 (op profit ex the 578 HAECO Americas disposal loss + ~1,050 D&A), T&I ~380, Head Office ~-636 and Healthcare ~-240. Drifts to 10.5% as the new Kunshan/Guangzhou bottling plants and Xiamen hangars load up and the loss-making HAECO Americas is gone.
base.capex_rationale: Non-property PPE capex ~7.2% of revenue FY2025 (group 5,595 less ~350 Swire Properties hotels + 109 intangibles), ~5.9% TTM. Elevated through 2028 by Swire Coca-Cola's RMB12bn ten-year plan and HAECO's >US$1bn four-year MRO expansion, then settles at 4.8% (D&A ex-ROU 4.1% plus growth capex for 2.5% nominal growth).
base.cash_tax_rationale: Blend of HK 16.5% (HAECO HK, T&I, Head Office), Chinese Mainland EIT 25% plus dividend withholding (Beverages' effective rate ~31% FY2025), Thailand/Vietnam 20%.
base.wc_rationale: Bottler and MRO: receivables + inventories exceed payables, so growth consumes working capital (negative capture on the revenue increase).

scenario_narratives.base: Swire Coca-Cola grows mid-single digits as Chinese Mainland demand recovers from the 2025 food-delivery-subsidy disruption and the new Kunshan, Guangzhou and Hainan plants absorb capacity, while aluminium/resin/fuel inflation from the Middle East conflict caps margin gains; HAECO keeps base-maintenance and engine work full on widebody utilisation, with the Xiamen Xiang'an hangars adding capacity from late 2026 and the HAECO Americas drag gone. Operating EBITDA margin edges from 10.1% to 10.5%; capex stays elevated through 2028 then normalises. Swire Properties and Cathay are held at today's market prices.
scenario_narratives.bull: Mainland consumer stimulus lifts bottling volumes and mix (sparkling, e-commerce channels), SE Asia franchises (Thailand, Vietnam) recover from tourism and competition pressure, and HAECO's capacity expansion plus the Vietnam JV pipeline drive high-single-digit revenue growth; margins reach 11.5% as new plants run at scale. Note the listed stakes are still at market in this scenario: the upside from a re-rating of Swire Properties toward NAV or a Cathay earnings step-up is NOT in the bull value and is shown instead in valuation_philosophy's look-through sensitivity.
scenario_narratives.bear: Chinese Mainland beverage demand stays soft under platform price wars, Thailand's sugar tax and weak tourism persist, commodity costs stay high and HAECO faces labour and material inflation it cannot pass through, so non-property revenue grows ~2% and EBITDA margin slips to 9.0%. Listed stakes are at market; a further leg down in HK office values (SP) or a fuel/demand shock at Cathay would compound this and is quantified in the look-through sensitivity, not in the bridge.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): Beverages margin is exposed to China consumer sentiment and commodity inflation simultaneously, and the 2025 Mainland disruption shows it can happen. Base 55%: the H1 2026 run-rate (Beverages attributable +5%, HAECO +9%) already supports it. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs Mainland volume recovery, SE Asia stabilisation and HAECO margin expansion all at once. The scenario spread is narrow because ~80% of gross asset value (the two listed stakes) is marked at market and identical in all three scenarios.

entry_price.method_note: The hurdle is applied to the operating-business flows only; the listed stakes, JVs, NCI and holdco net debt pass through the bridge at today's values. The entry price therefore answers 'what price earns 15% on the operating businesses if SP and Cathay are worth their market price', NOT 'what price earns 15% on the whole of Swire Pacific' -- the listed stakes earn whatever SP and Cathay shareholders earn.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Swire Pacific is valued as a sum of the parts because it is three different businesses under one ticker, and no single model fits all three. (1) Swire Properties (83.31%, separately listed) is an IAS-40 landlord whose reported profit is dominated by revaluation noise; the house method for it is AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity, but because it has its own liquid quote the stake is marked at market -- roughly half SP's own NAV, a deliberately conservative mark given HK Grade-A office oversupply. (2) Cathay (45.12%, equity-accounted) contributes accounting profit but only dividends in cash; it too is marked at market, net of the in-the-money value of the June-2026 exchangeable bond. (3) The consolidated non-property operating businesses -- Swire Coca-Cola, HAECO, Trading & Industrial, plus Healthcare and the Head Office cost centre -- are a standard owner-FCF DCF through the engine (HKD WACC 8%, leases charged in the flows, NCI deducted once in the bridge at value, SBC zero). Holdco net debt excludes Swire Properties' borrowings because SP enters at equity value. Underlying profit (ex revaluations) is the right earnings lens for reading the group, but it is not used as a flow here: capitalising group underlying profit would mix SP's post-interest property income, Cathay's non-cash equity income and the operating companies' pre-interest earnings at one rate. The finding is the gap between the A-share price and the sum of parts -- the conglomerate discount -- after Head Office costs have already been capitalised against the group. HOLDING-COMPANY DISCOUNT (added after the 2026-10-11 sanity check): the sum of parts is then cut by an explicit 35% discount to NAV (HK$8.52/B share in every scenario). Swire Pacific has never traded above 0.40x book in ten years (average 0.30x) even though its two largest assets have their own liquid quotes. The market has never paid look-through value for the stakes, and the reasons are structural: John Swire & Sons controls ~52% of votes through the B class, capital allocation sits with the family holdco (the HAECO Americas loss, a second Cathay recapitalisation, the Cathay exchangeable bond), the cash route from SP and Cathay is dividends only, and the B float is thin. 35% is the discount that brings the base value to the 10-year P/B ceiling. It is applied to NAV, not hidden in the WACC: the operating DCF stays at 8%, and the stakes stay at market.

look_through_sensitivity.note: Per 10% move in the 1972.HK / 0293.HK share price, holding everything else (11,723 / 6,743.9 and 3,874 / 6,743.9). SP at its own reported NAV (~2x market) would add roughly HK$17/B share; SP at -20% (another HK office leg down) removes ~HK$3.5. These swings dwarf the operating-business scenario spread and are why the three scenarios look tight.

key_risks_to_valuation: The holdco discount (35%, HK$8.52/B share) is the single largest judgement in the value. Every 5 percentage points is ~HK$1.22/B share. It is anchored on the 10-year P/B ceiling, not on an observed discount to SOTP, because no historical SOTP series exists in the filings.
Swire Properties is ~60% of gross asset value at market: a further de-rating on HK office vacancy (13.5-18% citywide) or Mainland retail moves the SOTP ~HK$1.74/B share per 10%.
Cathay stake (~20% of GAV) is a high-beta airline exposure to jet fuel (cost per ATK +18% YoY H1 2026) and demand shocks; a fuel spike can halve its price.
Conglomerate discount is persistent for HK family-controlled holdcos (John Swire & Sons controls ~52% of votes through the B shares); the discount to SOTP may never close.
Beverages margin squeezed by aluminium/PET/sugar costs and Mainland channel disruption; Thailand sugar tax.

Segment D&A, capex and lease splits are estimated from group totals less Swire Properties' share; the consolidated statements do not publish non-property capex directly (+/-0.5pp of revenue on capex is ~HK$0.8-1.0/B share).

B-share liquidity and control: the B class trades ~27% cheaper per unit of economics than the A share (0019.HK) because John Swire & Sons holds most of it; that discount can persist or widen, and B-share volume is thin. Valuation is economically identical to 0019.HK / 5.

holdco_discount.anchor: 10-year P/B ceiling 0.40x (FY2017 0.3985x); undiscounted SOTP implied ~0.62x on 30 Jun 2026 book of HK$39.49/B share (FY2025 HK$38.49)
holdco_discount.scenario_discount_sensitivity_note: The engine's equity bridge is the same in every scenario, so one discount (35%) is applied to all three and scenario risk stays in the operating flows. What other discounts would mean, on the base SOTP of HK$24.35/B: 20% (a shallow conglomerate discount; needs a governance or simplification catalyst such as a Cathay sell-down or an SP privatisation) -> ~HK$19.5; 35% (applied; at the 10-year P/B ceiling) -> ~HK$15.8; 51% (puts the value at the 10-year AVERAGE P/B of 0.30x) -> ~HK$11.9. The average is not used as the base because part of the historical P/B gap reflected Swire Properties' own discount to NAV, and that is already in the SOTP through the at-market SP mark. Using the average would count that discount twice.
holdco_discount.what_would_move_it: Narrower: buyback resumption at a discount, simplification (a Cathay stake sale, SP privatisation or special distribution), or a sustained re-rating of 0087.HK above 0.40x book. Wider: another capital call into Cathay, value-destructive M&A, or B-share liquidity drying up further.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (0087.HK B-share quote); 52-week range 11.17-15.80. Sibling quotes (0019.HK A share, 1972.HK, 0293.HK) from the same endpoint, same close.
